node.title: L1 Mersenne-checkpoint cyclotomic normal form
node.statement: On each of the nine surviving first-checkpoint rows, write N=p+1, n=mN, and k=qN+b with m in {4,8,16}. Multiplication by p sends (q,0) to (-q,0), sends (q,b) to (b-q-1,N-b) for b>0, and its square sends (q,b) to (q-2b,b). If S is the p-cyclotomic closure of [0,p-1] and g_b=gcd(2b,m), then (q,0) lies in S exactly for q=0, while (q,b) lies in S exactly when q is congruent to 0 or b-1 modulo g_b. The Fourier-complement sizes are 2N+1, 9N/2+1, and 37N/4+1. In particular N consecutive frequencies vanish, so every nonzero signed word has support at least N+1. A checkpoint pair has exact support 2N-2. This is a low-weight cyclic-code normal form, not a row exclusion or L1 bound.
